subsystems.name: Chassis organism
subsystems.role: the living platform that hosts the sensing circuit — usually a bacterium or yeast chosen for hardiness and safety.

subsystems.name: Sensing circuit
subsystems.role: detects a pollutant or condition and converts it into a biochemical signal.
parts: regulator protein that binds the target

subsystems.name: Reporter and output
subsystems.role: makes the detection visible or measurable.

subsystems.name: Biocontainment
subsystems.role: keeps the organism alive where intended and kills it if it escapes.

subsystems.name: Telemetry and reader
subsystems.role: turns the biological signal into continuous data for users.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target and chassis
buildSteps.detail: Decide which pollutant or condition to detect, and pick an organism that survives the intended environment — soil, water, air or a surface.

buildSteps.title: Find or engineer a sensor
buildSteps.detail: Borrow natural regulator proteins that already respond to the target, or evolve new ones by directed evolution and screening.

buildSteps.title: Design the genetic circuit
buildSteps.detail: Simulate the promoter, amplifier and reporter as a gene network so the response is strong, fast and not triggered by lookalike chemicals.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the DNA
buildSteps.detail: Order chemically synthesised DNA fragments and assemble them into a construct, codon-optimised for the chassis.

buildSteps.title: Transform and select
buildSteps.detail: Insert the construct into the organism and select the cells that took it up and behave as designed.

buildSteps.title: Tune and characterise
buildSteps.detail: Measure dose–response curves, detection limits, response time and drift over days.

buildSteps.title: Prove containment
buildSteps.detail: Confirm the kill switch and nutrient dependence hold under stress, and measure how fast the organism dies outside its intended niche.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and read out
buildSteps.detail: Immobilise the cells in a device, place it in the field, and stream readings — with a fate-and-transport study to check nothing spreads.

prerequisites.why: circuits of many genes must be ordered and assembled quickly and affordably.
predictable promoters, ribosome-binding sites and terminators let a design work the first time.

prerequisites.tech: Genetic circuit modelling and design software
prerequisites.why: living circuits behave unpredictably; simulation narrows the trial-and-error.
a monitoring organism must not survive, spread or swap genes if it escapes.
the biological signal is useless unless it can be measured continuously and sent remotely.

pathway.milestone: lab and small-scale whole-cell biosensors for specific toxins such as arsenic and mercury
pathway.unlocks: proof that engineered cells can report pollutants at useful sensitivity.

pathway.milestone: encapsulated sensor devices that survive weeks outdoors and transmit data
pathway.unlocks: real deployments at industrial sites, rivers and mine tailings.

pathway.milestone: field-tested biocontainment and regulatory frameworks for released organisms
pathway.unlocks: permission to monitor large areas, not just fenced test plots.

pathway.milestone: distributed living sensor networks for water, soil and air
pathway.unlocks: continuous, low-cost environmental surveillance instead of periodic sampling.
